#902. NI can draw on strong club form in key window

Northern Ireland are top of Nations League Group B2 after four games

Despite being together for 16 straight days only a month ago, when Northern Ireland players reconvened this week for Nations League fixtures against Ukraine and Hungary there was still plenty of catching up to do.

Whether it be Pierce Charles' incredible double-save of Jarrod Bowen's penalty to preserve a point for Queens Park Rangers against West Ham, Isaac Price putting his own spot-kick woe behind him back at West Bromwich Albion, or Terry Devlin's double for Portsmouth against Swansea, there have been memorable moments aplenty for Michael O'Neill's squad back in club colours.

Most pleasing to the manager, however, will likely be the game time currently enjoyed by his players.

O'Neill has never shied away from the importance of a player's club situation to their international ambitions and, almost four years after his return to the Northern Ireland job, the message has clearly hit home.

Of what is a 24-man squad for games against Ukraine on Saturday and Hungary three days later, nine players made either a permanent or loan switch during the summer.

And while once the former Stoke City boss had to heavily rely on players who were getting precious few minutes in between international windows, now the group is full of regulars across England top three divisions.

Excluding the uncapped trio of Dermot Mee, Eoin Kenny and Braiden Graham, the remainder of the panel for this double-header have averaged over 1,000 minutes of club action during the 2026-27 campaign.

Of that group, only Tom Atcheson, who has been carrying a knock, Paddy McNair, Kieran Morrison and Callum Marshall have started fewer than four games since the side's most recent international against Georgia last month.

Watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC Two NI from19:15 GMT; Listen on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster; Watch, listen, live text and clips on BBC Sport app & website

The next step, O'Neill feels, is to have more and more joining the likes of Conor Bradley, Daniel Ballard, Trai Hume and Shea Charles in the Premier League.

"There's a lot of players who are playing on a regular basis at their clubs, which is a real positive," said O'Neill, who is without Ballard, Bradley and Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill for this window through injuries.

"I think at this stage of their career they should be looking up. Our players that play in the Championship hopefully will have aspirations to play in the Premier League, and I think we have players that are capable of that.

"A lot of these players are still around that 20, 21, 22 age group but they're capable of taking that step.

"The more players we can get to the Premier League will help us as a nation, there's no doubt about that. I'm pleased where a lot of the players are at this minute in time but I still think individually with their clubs they've got a lot of scope to grow and develop as well."

Birthdays and broken lamps - at home with the Charles brothers

Kenny's background 'not that important' to O'Neill

Two of those playing at League One level this season are attackers Jamie Donley and Marshall, both at Luton Town under Jack Wilshere.

While a regular goalscorer remains elusive for O'Neill - the side have scored just once in their past four home games and that was a Donley penalty against Luxembourg - both have found the net at Kenilworth Road in recent weeks.

Donley, who is on loan from Tottenham Hotspur, plays in a deeper role at the club than the false nine position he occupies for Northern Ireland and has scored three times with two assists since a goalless four-game Nations League window across the end of September and start of October.

"I think Jamie has played well for us as a nine. He's different in terms of what you might look for in a profile as a nine. He comes and links the play and plays a little bit deeper," said O'Neill.

"I don't think you can compare, with all due respect, the chances that he may get playing for Luton in League One where they're a strong team, to playing for Northern Ireland at Nations League B. They're not overly comparable. It's not down to position for Jamie. It's what he brings to the team.

"The most important thing for me is that Jamie comes in confident to our camps. The fact that he's scoring goals at his club can only help him, regardless of what position we play him in."

Marshall is one of the few in the squad still struggling for starts at club level, although he has found the net four times in League One since joining the Hatters from West Ham in the summer.

The 21-year-old, who had previous loan spells at West Brom, Huddersfield Town and Vfl Bochum, has featured just once in Northern Ireland's past five games and is yet to score at international level.

"I encouraged him to make the move [to Luton] on a permanent basis because I think that you go through a loan scenario and it's difficult," said O'Neill.

"I've been on the other side of that as a manager and brought players in on loan so I know that sometimes it's not always in the best interest of the player.

"Callum going to Luton, I think, was positive with the fact that Jack Wilshere really wanted him and they obviously had to pay a decent fee for him.

"It's now down to Callum really. He's at a club that I think should suit him as a striker. Callum is capable of scoring goals and the ball's in his court now."

#901. ‘An eternal shame’: Bilic and Croatia aim to use 7-0 humbling as fuel against England

The home humiliation last month has left a scar on Croatian football but their manager wants them to use it to positive effect in the Wembley rematch

As Croatia prepare to face England at Wembley on Thursday in the Nations League, wounds from a humiliating defeat by the same opponents last month are fresh and there is a lingering feeling of unease.

No one will say it – certainly not Slaven Bilic, who always believes in achieving goals that may seem unreachable to most others – but the impression is that Croatia would be satisfied to accept another defeat, provided it was gentle enough by score and hard‑fought by approach; that this game is not so much about the points as the (self-)respect they can regain.

Croatia lost 7-0 against England in Rijeka and were lucky not to concede more. After the game, Roy Keane commented that England looked as if they were matched against junior players, but that wasn’t it, and neither was the comparison to San Marino or Andorra pushed widely through the media here.

Croatia did not look like a weak or inadequate team – they did not look like a team at all. The best assessments about the game came from within that night. “I have to say this,” the captain, Luka Modric, said. “I’ve been here for 20 years and this is the first time I feel ashamed. You can lose the game; that is not the issue here – they are simply better than us at the moment. But to squander the reputation we worked so hard and so long building – that is unacceptable.”

Bilic agreed: “We were no match for them in any respect: challenges, aggression, technique, physicality … And then, of course, your confidence, your focus and your mental resolve all drop and everything falls apart.”

It seemed that even the head coach, known for his eloquence and persuasive style of communication, struggled to comprehend what had happened and to find the right words. “I am left with an eternal shame,” Bilic said in a later interview. But then there was a moment of unusual clarity, when he was asked what he had told the players in the dressing room.

“I told them that there are games which you simply need to forget and turn a new page as soon as possible, because you have the next match in a few days. But this is not one of those games. This one you should never forget. You should keep it in mind for the rest of your lives and always be reminded of it so that you do everything not to repeat something like that ever again.”

The question on everyone’s mind, even if they dare not admit it, is: what if there is a repeat?

The team responded well to the England implosion, producing a battling display against Spain three days later. Although Croatia lost, it was a close game and the world champions were pushed hard before Ivan Perisic was sent off after 79 minutes, with the score 1-1, for a second yellow card that means he is unavailable for the Wembley rematch with England.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

It was a good way to start their redemption but England pose challenges of a different kind. The weight is not only mental but very much physical. Bilic made some serious mistakes with his team selection and tactics in Rijeka and the players’ resolve was nowhere near the required level even before “everything fell apart”. But the way England play – when they play well – creates a clear mismatch for a team that still revolve around a 41‑year‑old playmaker, with no true defensive midfielder or top wingers; much more so than Spain’s methodical approach.

England may simply be too fast for Croatia, and Bilic faces the immense task of somehow slowing them, limiting their attacking capacity and reducing the game to isolated incidents as much as possible. He needs to be pragmatic, which may include heavier involvement for one of his assistants, the set-piece specialist Gianni Vio, but first and foremost the players need to show much more grit and intensity.

So get stuck in? Well, yes. That is what the public back home wants to see, rather than some clever idea Bilic may have up his sleeve. “We can hardly wait,” Bilic said, but he was uncharacteristically vague and avoided going into details about the team’s ambitions.

The real issue is proving that Croatia, despite the recent haunting trauma, are still a true team: one worthy of the glorious past and with hope for the future.

#900. Shirt pull on Isak should have been penalty - panel

Alexander Isak (centre) has scored seven goals in nine Premier League games for Liverpool this season

Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty against Arsenal after Alexander Isak was pulled back by Jurrien Timber, the Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel has ruled.

Isak just failed to get his head on the end of a cross by Bradley Barcola in the 21st minute of the game at Anfield on 1 November.

Referee Andy Madley did not award a penalty and it was checked and cleared by video assistant referee (VAR) Stuart Attwell, but replays showed Timber grabbed Isak's shirt.

The KMI Panel voted 4:1 that the penalty should have been awarded on the field, with a 3:2 vote that the VAR should have intervened and sent the referee to the pitchside monitor.

Arsenal led 1-0 at the time through Kai Havertz, which proved to be the only goal of the game.

Two panellists highlighted the "subjectivity in assessing impact" as a reason not to intervene, but the majority view was that it was a "clear and obvious error" by the VAR.

The KMI Panel unanimously voted that Timber's challenge did not warrant a red card for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

Isak stayed on his feet during the incident.

After the match, Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola told BBC Match of the Day: "There is a clear grab of the shirt.

"Alex was just in front of him. He was going to head in front of the goal, but couldn't because he grabbed the shirt.

"If he goes to the floor, they call the penalty, 100%. It should be like this, but it is what it is.

"Next time, the managers should tell Alex to go to the floor, otherwise they won't call it.

"The answer is you have to dive. If you don't dive they won't call it."

The KMI Panel ruled that there was a second VAR error on 31 October.

It said Ipswich should have been awarded a penalty against Hull City when Nobel Mendy held back Dara O'Shea at a corner.

Referee Peter Bankes did not spot the offence and VAR Neil Davies took no action.

The game was 0-0 at the time. Ipswich took the lead shortly afterwards and it finished 2-2.

#899. Pete Davidson Teases Future Tattoos After “Brutal” Removal Process

As Saturday Night Live alum Pete Davidson continues his tattoo removal journey, he shared insight into the “brutal” process in an exclusive E! News interview at the How to Rob a Bank premiere.

Pete Davidson is wearing his heart on his sleeve—just not in ink.

As the Saturday Night Live alum continues his tattoo removal journey, which he began in 2020, he shared a cheeky update about where he stands in the process.

“It’s brutal,” Davidson told E! News in exclusive interview at the How to Rob a Bank New York premiere alongside costar Nicholas Hoult. “I’ve only been wearing for sweaters for, like, six months so you don’t know what’s going on under there.”

But while Davidson—dad to daughter Scottie, 11 months, with ex Elsie Hewitt—has gotten his once sleeved-up arms to nearly completely bare skin, the King of Staten Island star quipped of his tattoos, “You never know, they might come back.”

That wasn’t the only teasing, however, he provided.

While the whole world seems to be waiting to know who the next James Bond star might be, the 32-year-old joked fans shouldn’t look much further than Davidson—Pete Davidson.

Ignoring Hoult at his side—who has been rumored to be circling the role alongside Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor—the Bodies Bodies Bodies alum revealed, “It’s going to be me.”

“Plot twist,” Davidson quipped. “I will be the first American James Bond.”

Jokes aside though, Davidson offered his full support to Hoult—who remained as elusive on the topic as the character itself.

“If anyone should get it, it’s this guy next to me,” Davidson mused. “He’s the best guy for the job.”

And that’s not the only role Davidson says Hoult would ace. In fact, the comedian admitted his costar—who shares three kids with wife Bryana Holly—has been a great role model during Davidson's his first year of fatherhood.

“Very supportive and checks in,” Davidson said of Hoult. “We both check in on each other’s families and see how they’re doing because that’s what friends do.”

Meanwhile, Davidson previously shared that his entire life perspective has shifted nearly a year after welcoming his baby girl.

“My priorities have shifted in just that becoming a dad is great for so many reasons,” Davidson told E! News in an interview earlier this year, “but it just made me realize the stuff that I cared about so much don't actually matter.”

The Bupkis alum considered that becoming a dad has “calmed” him. As he put it, “I'm just happy where I am.”

While Davidson is cooling down and removing his tattoos, other stars have debuted quite the body art over the years. Keep reading for the most inked up celebrities, and don’t miss How to Rob a Bank when it hits theaters Nov. 13.

After shaving off some of his hair, the Aquaman star revealed a new head tattoo in September 2022 that he said has been "20 years in the making."

The "Karma" singer unveiled a bicep tattoo of a teddy bear with angel wings in June 2024. The design was a nod to the cover art of her Guilty Pleasure album.

In April 2024, the "Ex's and Oh's" singer debuted a new tattoo—located on her rear—that paid tribute to some very important men in her life.

"I always said I'd get my baby daddys name tattooed on my butt…so I did," Elle, who is the daughter of Rob Schneider, wrote on Instagram. "I got 'brethren' for the men helping me raise my son. I love you guys so much, I wouldn't want to do life without yall."

The "Genesis" singer unveiled her large face tattoo in October 2022, sharing that she spent 10 years "emotionally working up" to it.

The Blink-182 drummer got a tattoo reading "Time Flies" in August 2023 after taking his 30th flight since surviving his 2008 plane crash.

In March 2023, the Twilight actor and his wife got matching tattoos honoring their wedding date.

The Selling Sunset star debuted a face tattoo, which read "invincible" in script and sits beneath her jawline, in April 2022.

The "Stitches" singer debuted a tattoo on the back of his neck in March 2022.

After filming Game of Thrones' final season, the actress added some symbolic ink to her tattoo collection in loving memory of her character Arya Stark.

Forever MOD! The Game Of Thrones star permanently inked a dragon tattoo on her wrist after wrapping the final season of the show.

While celebrating their engagement in 2018, the Jonas Brothers singer and the Game of Thrones alum got matching Toy Story tattoos. The pair broke up in 2023 after four years of marriage.

#898. Referee observer banned for discriminatory comments

Brian Curson has been involved in football for more than 40 years

A Pro Ref referee observer has been suspended for nine weeks and fined Â£200 for making discriminatory remarks after a match he was working at.

Brian Curson had visited Kenilworth Road to assess the officials at the League One fixture between Luton Town and Rotherham United on 15 November 2025.

An allegation was made that Curson made two discriminatory comments in the lounge at Luton's stadium after the game, which led to the Football Association investigation.

Curson was charged with acting in an improper manner and/or using abusive and/or insulting words.

It was considered an 'aggravated breach', using words which included a reference - whether express or implied - to ethnic origin, race or nationality.

Curson, who no longer works for Pro Ref, said that he did not recall making the comments but the FA commission "was satisfied on the balance of probabilities" that they had been made.

The FA requested a time-based sanction because of Curson's role in the sport, as a player would serve a suspension of between nine and 12 matches.

It was determined that, taking into account Curson's experience and role on the day of the match, he should be suspended for nine weeks.

Curson was also told he must attend a mandatory education programme, and received a warning as to future conduct.

#897. Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge

Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers

Mail us with all of your questions and answers

“Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?”

A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband.

But if that Chelsea team are not themselves the best answer that Knowledge has come up with, they are at least associated with them, having been knocked out of the Champions League by José Mourinho’s captain-strewn Inter. Inter ended up beating Bayern Munich 2-0 in the final, with a team that included the then full-time captains of Brazil (Lúcio), Romania (Cristian Chivu), Cameroon (Samuel Eto’o) and Macedonia (Goran Pandev), while the captain of Serbia (Dejan Stankovic) came off the bench to replace Chivu in the second half and Pandev was replaced by Sulley Muntari, who while not Ghana’s full-time captain had led the side in their most recent game, a 2-1 defeat at Bosnia and Herzegovina that March.

But that’s not all! Among the unused substitutes was Iván Córdoba, who at this point in his career had lost Colombia’s armband to Mario Yepes but been given it back for their previous game, against Paraguay, in the absence of his fellow centre-back. Also in the team and worthy of note, if not of inclusion in our tally of then captains, were Wesley Sneijder, occasional Netherlands skipper and still their all-time record appearance maker, and Javier Zanetti, who regularly captained Argentina and is No 4 on their list of all-time appearance makers (he would be higher had he not been frozen out by their then manager, Diego Maradona, before the 2010 World Cup), with occasional Kenya captain McDonald Mariga also among the subs.

By our count that’s seven players in one matchday squad who could boast of being their country’s current captain at kick-off, and none of whom captained their club side – that honour went to Zanetti. Our searches have not found another team to match that one, but readers have suggested a couple who came close, in the shape of Tottenham in 2020-21 (who boasted five international captains at the time in Hugo Lloris of France; Serge Aurier of Côte d’Ivoire; South Korea’s Son Heung-min; Gareth Bale of Wales; and England’s own Harry Kane, suggested by John Curry) and Liverpool just last year, when in Conor Bradley, Andy Robertson, Virgil van Dijk, Wataru Endo, Mo Salah and Dominik Szoboszlai they had six – though they never played together while they were all incumbent international captains. Any more for any more?

The fastest former footballer we found in time for last week’s instalment was Alexei Smertin, the former Russia and Chelsea midfielder, who screamed around the Kazan Marathon course in 2020 in just two hours, 48 minutes and 17 seconds. But as Richard Askham emailed to point out, that has since been bettered by Joe Skarz, formerly of Bury, Rotherham and Oxford United, and current manager of Golcar United of the Northern Counties East League Premier Division, who in 2025 finished the Yorkshire Marathon with a chip time of 2hr 47min 33sec.

The next question is what level of football do you need to reach to qualify as a footballer? Because Stig Lindmark tipped us off about the former AIK academy player Andreas Almgren, whose dreams of football glory were derailed by injury in his teens and eventually shifted his focus towards distance running. In New York at the start of this month – while the retired cyclist Tom Dumoulin was putting most former footballers to shame with a time of 2:27:12 – he ran his first ever marathon and only went and won the thing, in 2hr 6min 1sec. With no senior competitive appearances he probably does not count, but it’s a good enough effort to get a mention.

“Has a headed goal ever been awarded goal of the season,” wonders Rupert Sheard. “I can think of a few belters, but awards tend to go to ones kicked in.”

“The closest I could get was Robin van Persie’s flying header at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, for the Netherlands against Spain,” writes Sinan Eccles. “He was pipped to the official goal of the tournament by James Rodríguez’s iconic volley, but did make it to third in that year’s Puskas Award – behind Rodríguez and Stephanie Roche.”

Peter Tomlin writes: “Having researched the goal of the season awards in many countries, the only header I could find that won was Keith Houchen’s fantastic one in the 1986-87 FA Cup Final for Coventry v Tottenham. However, Alisson’s dramatic 95th-minute headed winner v West Brom was voted Liverpool’s goal of the season for the 2020-21 season.”

And Mark Johnson points out that Basile Boli’s ridiculous bullet header for Marseille against PSG at the end of the 1993 season would surely have won the Ligue 1 goal of the season award but for the inconvenient fact that no such award existed at the time.

Martyn Amos has responded to last week’s scepticism about the possibility of an Ipswich fan website existing in 1990, the year before the first known website went online. “Just to clarify, the original page was set up by Phil Clarke, who was working at BT Labs in Martlesham (near Ipswich), in 1990,” he writes. “At the time, as I said, the web was still experimental, and I think the page was only available internally. Your correspondent is correct in saying that the first public website appeared in August 1991. But the ITFC page still existed, in some recognisable form, using the standard web technology, in 1990, so I think it counts. That’s my understanding, anyway.”

With Lee Power taking charge of Swindon Town, in last week’s Knowledge archive we dug up our piece from 2006 on chairs acting as managers, we wrote in October 2015. Neil Bellis, the director of communications at Chester FC, writes to point out we missed Terry Smith off our list.

“He took over four games into the season despite not really knowing much about ‘soccer’,” writes Neil. “He was a former American Football coach but for some reason ending up buying our club. Not only did we end up getting relegated from the Football League for the first time in 1999-2000 we also saw a few very strange ideas from him including having a team talk as the Lord’s prayer and appointing a captain in defence, midfield and attack. Thankfully we are now fan owned so this level of insanity shouldn’t happen again.”

One of Smith’s first games as manager was against Aston Villa in the League Cup, a fixture that prompted a visit from ITV to see what was going on. The result of that visit can be seen here:

“There’s nothing magical about being a coach,’ said Smith not long after his arrival. “It’s like being the general manager of a business, the coaching principles are the same in any sport.” That doesn’t sound too promising but things didn’t really go horribly wrong until the end of November, when Chester began a run of 11 defeats in 12 matches. There’s some footage here of the aftermath of the 5-1 home defeat by Leyton Orient just after Christmas – “I want to thank you guys,” says Smith in the dressing room. “That’s the most pitiful, pitiful effort I’ve ever damn seen.”

Smith stepped down as manager and brought in Ian Atkins in January 2000, then sold the club in October 2001.

“What’s the highest score by a team or in a match where no player scored more than one goal?” writes Paul Gage.

“Manchester United have 20 league titles, won by three managers. Liverpool have 20 league titles won by 10. Which teams have the most and fewest titles won by the most and fewest managers?” asks Will Marquand.

“Djed Spence (shirt No 99) set up Pio Esposito (No 94) in Inter’s 2-0 win over Como at the weekend. Has there ever been a combination for a goal (assist and scorer) with a higher combined shirt number than 193?” writes Joe Strawson.

“Did the Fenerbahce side have more combined Premier League appearances than Liverpool in the teams’ recent Champions League match? If so was this the first instance of a club in Europe playing opposition who had more game appearances in their own league than they had themselves?” ponders Josh Wolff-Martin.

#896. Overeem vs Manuwa added to Jake Paul's Christmas Eve fight card

Alistair Overeem makes his professional boxing debut against Britain's Jimi Manuwa in a six-round heavyweight bout on the Christmas Eve card headlined by Jake Paul in Dubai; the YouTuber-turned boxer returns against Cedric Doumbe, 12 months on from having his jaw broken by Anthony Joshua

Alistair Overeem will make his professional boxing debut against Britain's Jimi Manuwa as the MMA stars collide on Jake Paul's comeback show on Christmas Eve.

Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) have confirmed that Overeem, known as 'The Demolition Man', and 'Poster Boy' Manuwa will meet in a six-round professional heavyweight boxing bout on the undercard of Paul's cruiserweight clash with Cedric Doumbe in Dubai.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Former Strikeforce heavyweight champion and K-1 World Grand Prix winner Overeem said: "I've fought the best in the world, and I've been a world champion in multiple disciplines. Now I'm starting a new chapter in boxing, and I'm not here to make up the numbers.

"Jimi Manuwa is a dangerous man with serious knockout power, but I've built my career on taking the toughest challenges in combat sports"

Manuwa, who began his professional MMA career in 2008, won his first 14 professional fights before establishing himself among the UFC's most dangerous strikers.

He retired from MMA in 2019 with a 17-6 record, with 15 of his 17 victories coming by knockout or technical knockout. The 46-year-old returned to competition in August 2026, making a successful professional boxing debut with a second-round TKO victory over former UFC heavyweight Chase Sherman.

Manuwa said: "London is in everything I do. Where I come from, pressure makes you, and it makes me.

"I've watched Alistair since I was coming up, and I know exactly what he's capable of. That's why I wanted this fight.

"After my win in Orlando, I wasn't looking for an easy opponent. On Christmas Eve, one of us is going to sleep, and it's not going to be me."

Overeem vs Manuwa adds another explosive encounter to the card headlined by global superstar Paul, on his return to the ring a year on from suffering a broken jaw in a sixth-round stoppage loss to former two-time unified heavyweight world champion Anthony Joshua.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

MVP chief executive Nakisa Bidarian said: "Netherlands' Alistair Overeem and the United Kingdom's Jimi Manuwa are two of the most recognisable names in combat sports, with decades of experience competing against the best in the world and a combined 40 knockouts in MMA.

"Bringing these two legends together in a professional boxing match adds another compelling matchup to an already massive Christmas Eve event.

"With Jake Paul facing Cedric Doumbe in the main event, we're assembling a card that brings together some of the biggest personalities and most dangerous strikers in combat sports for fans in Dubai and around the world."

News. So, much like you might meet up with coworkers from your first job, they make it a point to get happy hours (and the occasional major reunion) on their calendar. Equal parts intriguing and covetable, this pairing was solidified at The Comedy Central Roast of Justin Bieber in 2015 before they teamed up for their VH1 cooking show, Martha & Snoop's Potluck Dinner Party. "She different, ya know, than what I'm accustomed," the marijuana-loving 17-time Grammy winner told LA Weekly of the Westchester-based domestic doyenne. 'Cause it feels like holy matrimony, and not holy macaroni."

Theirs is a newer alliance, but no less desirable. After years of existing in the same orbit, the "Hotline Bling" rapper and the "Hello" songstress, who have over a dozen Grammys between them, began throwing out the idea of a collaboration. "I really want us to do an official remix," she told Canada's etalk of their well-coordinated hits. "I love Drake. I love Drake so much. I even got the coat that's in the video, I got it delivered the other day, I ordered it. The red one." He responded by saying, "I'd do anything with Adele. I'd literally go to Adele's house right now and do laundry for her." Instead, they grabbed a bite to eat and hit up an L.A. bowling alley. Next time, you know, call us on our cell phone.

#894. How promotion, relegation and knockouts work in Nations League

England are closing in on reaching the knockout rounds of the 2026-27 Uefa Nations League

England go into their final two 2026-27 Nations League matches on the brink of qualification for the quarter-finals.

Thomas Tuchel's side sit second after four matches in Group A3, with a point in either of their final two matches in November against Croatia and Spain enough to secure a place in the final eight teams.

November's international break is the final two full rounds of matches, with four rounds already complete.

The eight teams to finish in the top two of the four League A groups will play in the knockout rounds that start in March 2027.

Teams finishing at the top of groups in leagues B and C will earn promotion for the next Nations League cycle, while teams that finish second in a League B or League C group will face either a third-placed or bottom-placed team from the league above them in a promotion/relegation play-off.

The two worst sides to finish bottom of a League A group are automatically relegated. The other bottom sides in League A, third-placed sides in League A and bottom-placed sides in League B are at risk of relegation.

The losers of the play-offs will be relegated.

As the Nations League format is changing for the next cycle, taking place across 2028 and 2029, all League D teams are guaranteed promotion to League C.

Additionally, no teams from League C will be relegated at the end of this cycle.

The new format will consist of three larger leagues, meaning there will not be a League D in the next campaign.

Portugal and Spain are the only sides guaranteed to play in the quarter-finals at present, having both won their opening four matches.

England, who are three points behind Spain in Group A3, are six points clear of third-placed Croatia and with a significantly superior head-to-head record. Unless England were to lose 7-0 or worse to Croatia on Thursday, the Three Lions will be certain of a place in the last eight.

In Group A1, France and Italy sit in the top two spots. Belgium are a point behind Italy in third. Two of those three sides will advance to the quarter-finals.

It is a similar tale in Group A2. Netherlands and Greece are the top two, three points clear of Germany in third. With Serbia bottom on zero points, two of the current top three will advance.

In A4, Denmark are second and three points clear of Wales and Norway. One of the trio will join table-toppers Portugal.

The quarter-finals are played across two legs in March's international break.

The winners of each tie will advance to the semi-finals in June 2027, which are played in a one-off match across Wednesday 9 and Thursday 10 June. The final takes place on Sunday, 13 June.

Wales are in a three-way battle alongside Norway and Denmark to qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals

While England's League A campaign has gone well so far, Wales' has been trickier.

In a tough group with Portugal, Denmark and Norway, Wales have picked up three points from four games after beating Norway 2-1 in Cardiff.

With Portugal already qualified for the last eight, Wales will need close to maximum points in their final matches against Norway and Portugal to stand any chance of making the last eight.

A third-place finish would put them in a play-off to avoid relegation in March, while coming last in the group may ensure a drop down to League B.

Scotland are now unable to reach the top spot in Group B1 and are unlikely to make the promotion/relegation play-offs.

In order to finish second, Scotland need to win both of their final two games and hope Slovenia pick up no more than a point from theirs. Alternatively, Scotland can pick up four points and finish second, providing Slovenia lose their final two matches.

Northern Ireland have had a successful international break with two wins, two draws and no goals conceded in their four matches in Group B2.

They sit top of the group by a point, with their remaining matches against bottom side Ukraine and second-place Hungary.

Should they beat Ukraine and Hungary fail to beat Georgia in November's first round of fixtures, they will guarantee top spot and promotion. A win for them and Hungary doing the same would mean the two sides face off in a promotion-decider in the final round of games.

The Republic of Ireland are third in Group B3 following five points from their first four matches.

Their remaining two fixtures are against the top two teams Austria and Kosovo. Wins in both would guarantee a top-two finish and would also put them in a strong position to win the group, depending on goal difference and the result of Austria's meeting with Israel.

Spain are the current holders of the European Championship, beating England in the 2024 final

Once the Nations League campaign is concluded, all 54 competing nations will be ranked based on their performance in this edition of the competition.

That ranking will have a direct impact on qualification for the 2028 European Championships, being held in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

The Nations League ranking will also determine the seeding of nations for Euro 2028 qualification.

Regular qualifying will take place between March and November 2027, with play-offs for the remaining spots in the tournament to take place in March 2028.

As there are four co-hosts and none of them have been granted immediate qualification, the number of how many qualify will effectively determine how many play-off spots will be up for grabs.

Uefa have said that up to two places will be given to the best-ranked co-hosts that fail to qualify for the tournament via its primary qualification route.

Scenarios have already been designed for occurrences where either two, one or zero co-hosts are given entry spots.

Depending on which play-off format is required, either eight or 12 teams will enter.

A total of 24 teams will enter the European Championships, 20 of them will consist of the winners of the 12 qualifying groups and the eight best runners-up from those group.

The remaining runners-up will enter the play-offs, alongside the Nations League group winners from League A, League B and League C that failed to finish in the top two of their Euro 2028 qualifying group.

If extra teams are required, the best-ranked League D group winner will enter the play-offs.

Any additional play-off spots that become available after that will filter down to the next-highest ranked Nations League finishers until the play-off spots are filled.

#893. ‘Hear the goals during the afterlife’: Barça fans get to inter ashes at club’s new memorial

Memorial FC Barcelona, part of upgrade to Camp Nou stadium, will consist of 26,000 niches where fans can deposit their ashes

Lifelong supporters of Barcelona football club will soon be able to cheer on the club from beyond the grave – but, like everything else at Barça, eternal devotion comes at a price.

As part of an upgrade to the Camp Nou, the club has inaugurated the Memorial FC Barcelona, consisting of 26,000 niches where fans can deposit their ashes after their own final whistle has blown.

Supporting the team from the afterlife will cost €2,490 (£2,082) for 10 years or €6,000 for 50 years, with an annual maintenance fee of €70. Guaranteeing your niche for eternity will set you back €10,000, with a further €490 for a memorial plaque.

Presenting the Memorial FC Barcelona, María Elena Fort, the club’s institutional vice-president, said: “When my grandfather died many years ago, he said the only thing he wanted was to be buried next to Barça’s pitch so that he could hear the goals go in during the afterlife. Many fans dream of the same thing.”

The memorial, designed by the architect Quique Montoya, will consist of four large illuminated squares, while the memorial plaques will be installed in a glass wall backlit with LED lights. The urns will be kept behind a mural commemorating key moments in the club’s 125-year history.

The rival Spanish clubs Atlético Madrid, Betis and Espanyol already have smaller columbariums in their stadiums.

Work on Barcelona’s will begin late next year and the club says more than 1,000 Barça fans have already booked their place. Their contributions will go towards paying the huge cost of redeveloping the stadium, which was built in 1957.

In 2023, the club embarked on a scheme to increase capacity from 99,354 to 105,000 – 15,000 more than Wembley Stadium and making it the second biggest football venue in the world, after the Rungrado 1st of May Stadium in Pyongyang in North Korea.

The cost of the changes, initially costed at €900m, is now approaching €2bn, now being borne by non-season ticket holders who have seen ticket prices double in recent years.

The work, being carried out by the Turkish firm Limak Construction, has been plagued by delays and labour disputes. In 2024, FC Barcelona recognised that, among other abuses, more than 1,000 subcontractors had not been paid for overtime.

Work is due to be completed later this year but the club will have to play part of next season at the Olympic Stadium (capacity 55,926) while a roof is installed on Camp Nou.

#892. Does Pickford finally face serious competition for his England place?

England head coach Thomas Tuchel used long-time first choice Jordan Pickford (left) and James Trafford (right) during the previous international break

When England head coach Thomas Tuchel decided to pick Leeds United goalkeeper James Trafford to face World Cup holders Spain at Wembley in the last international break, it sparked the first stirrings about preparations for life without long-time first choice Jordan Pickford.

Tuchel made it clear Pickford was still England's number one pick, but the simple fact he decided to alternate keepers - playing Trafford in the 3-2 loss to Spain then victory against Czech Republic, before Everton's 32-year-old returned for the Wembley win against the Czechs and the 7-0 rout in Croatia - created intrigue and debate.

England meet Croatia at Wembley on Thursday before facing the biggest test of their Uefa Nations League campaign when they play Spain in Madrid on Sunday.

Tuchel maintains strong faith in Pickford, an outstanding performer for England, but Trafford has at least had the chance to stake his claim.

Tuchel has suggested he may use a rotation system for the pair once more in the upcoming internationals, which will only increase scrutiny on England's goalkeeping position.

Pickford's record is outstanding since he made his debut in a 0-0 draw against Germany at Wembley in 2017.

In his time as first choice, England have once more emerged as major players on global stage, reaching the World Cup semi-finals in 2018 and 2026, as well as successive Euros finals at the delayed 2020 tournament and Euro 2024.

Measured by Opta stats, Pickford has made only two errors leading to goals in 93 appearances, with 46 clean sheets and a 74% save ratio.

Trafford's international career is in its infancy and, while former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson says Pickford remains Tuchel's undisputed first choice, he believes the head coach's recent strategy is a sensible one.

Robinson told BBC Sport: "It obviously remains to be seen what Thomas Tuchel does in these two England games, but I could see exactly what he was doing by giving James Trafford game time in the last round of matches.

"We are so guilty as a nation of taking one goalkeeper to a tournament who has 70, 80, 90 caps, then the two of three below him could have less than double figures combined."

Robinson's point is proved by the statistic that 80 of Pickford's appearances have been competitive games, with 33 at major tournaments, made up of 19 at the World Cup and 14 at European Championships.

"Competitive and tournament caps give you the type of experience you can't get as a number two or three keeper," said Robinson.

"James Trafford is only 24 and has four caps - two of them competitive - so you can see exactly what Tuchel is doing, looking ahead to a situation where England's recognised number one is not available to him, or there is a drop off in form.

"We saw the last selections and all thought Jordan Pickford's place is under threat and James Trafford is going to be the next number one. I don't think Thomas Tuchel saw it as starkly or simply as that.

"It's a conversation that will definitely take place down the road, but not now. Jordan is England's first choice, in my opinion, rightfully so given his consistency and performances over such a long period.

"This is a debate and conversation for the future definitely because Father Time catches up with everyone eventually and the manager needs to have a contingency plan, but Jordan Pickford very much remains number one and Thomas Tuchel has said as much.

"I don't think Jordan Pickford is under threat for his jersey on a permanent basis any time soon, irrespective of the next selection, but what Tuchel is doing reinforces the impression that he has to be at the top of his game and maintain high standards, which he certainly has been doing when I've watched him this season.

"The biggest compliment I can pay Jordan Pickford is that when you have got that England goalkeeper's shirt, everybody thinks somebody else should be doing it. I know that from personal experience.

"You're there to be shot at, but there has been no noise around Jordan Pickford for a very long time now.

"It has worked both ways for Jordan, James and Thomas Tuchel, and worked very well. Jordan knows he can't rest on his laurels and he will just play regardless. He has to be playing well.

"Is James Trafford challenging Jordan Pickford right now? Yes he is - if Jordan Pickford isn't playing very well and Jordan Pickford is making errors.

"None of the above are true right now because he's playing well for Everton and has done nothing wrong for England."

Robinson also drew on club form to support Pickford's case. Since the start of the 2024-25 season, only Arsenal's title-winning keeper David Raya has more clean sheets in the league than Pickford at Everton.

Raya has 39 clean sheets in that time, while Pickford has 27, with Robinson saying: "That's a superb record and all logic tells you Pickford will have to work a lot harder for his clean sheets than David Raya."

Trafford staked his claim in those Nations League games against Spain and the Czech Republic, putting him at the forefront of Tuchel's thoughts as the main understudy to Pickford.

Crystal Palace's Dean Henderson is now back in contention after injury and hoping to add to his six caps, although he has not been included in Tuchel's latest squad.

Trafford moved to Leeds United from Manchester City in the summer in a British record deal for a goalkeeper that could be worth up to Â£45m.

It came after a Â£23m move to City from Burnley the previous summer, when his hopes of becoming Pep Guardiola's first choice were unexpectedly ended by the decision to sign Gianluigi Donnarumma from Paris St-Germain.

Robinson said: "James Trafford needed that move to Leeds United and Leeds United needed a keeper of his level. This is a match made in heaven.

"And don't forget, in a Premier League career with Burnley, Manchester City and Leeds United, Trafford has only played 42 Premier League games â just a little more than a full season â and one Champions League game. He needs this experience.

"He's got a huge amount of potential, with his quality, all-round goalkeeping and mental approach. He has the potential be England's future number one, which Tuchel clearly sees him to be.

"He has the mentality to reach the very top, which is very difficult because not all goalkeepers have that. It's a tough place to be, a very lonely place to be, but he has the ability to cope with that situation.

"I was at Bournemouth when he made an error in the Leeds United defeat there, but, knowing the type of character he, is it won't faze him. It won't bother him. Because of his personality and his character traits, he has got the ability to go right to the top.

"You'd think Dean Henderson will be back in the squad in due course once he has played more games.

"Jason Steele is in there again, but he's a mentor figure behind the scenes, not someone who will ever start or threaten the established goalkeepers.

"If you rewind back 18 or 24 months, you had Nick Pope, Sam Johnstone, James Trafford, Dean Henderson, Aaron Ramsdale and Jordan Pickford - a real plethora of England goalkeepers.

"Now Nick Pope is not playing at Newcastle United, Sam Johnstone's not in the equation and Aaron Ramsdale is nowhere near."

Ramsdale's decline has been dramatic after leaving Arsenal for Southampton in August 2024, with a loan spell at Newcastle United proving to be unsuccessful. He has effectively been fourth choice at Saints this season, failing to make matchday squads.

Robinson said: "I find Aaron Ramsdale's situation very sad because I believe he's a goalkeeper able to play at the top level.

"He should be in this conversation because he's a goalkeeper I really like, but he's been very unfortunate with selection of clubs and the way their season have gone. I still think there is time for him to come back into the reckoning.

"For now, though, if there is a conversation to be had about England's goalkeepers, then Jordan Pickford and James Trafford is that conversation, with Jordan still very much the number one right now as far as I'm concerned."

#891. Brenda Song Says Suite Life Cast Was “Underpaid and Overworked”

Brenda Song shared why it felt like she and her Suite Life of Zack & Cody costars were “underpaid and overworked” by Disney Channel, noting it felt like the cast actually paid the network.

Brenda Song’s bank account isn’t as suite as it could be.

The Suite Life of Zack & Cody star reflected on her time on Disney Channel, noting that it felt like she and her costars’ checked in for hard work but checked out with little to show for it.

As Song told her costar Dylan Sprouse on the Nov. 10 episode of his Wildmen podcast, “I look at that time and I was like, we paid them.”

And while the 38-year-old emphasized she had a “lovely time” playing hotel heiress London Tipton from 2005 to 2011 on Suite Life and its spinoff series The Suite Life on Deck, there’s one qualm that is still setting sail.

As she sees it, “The only thing that was hard about that time was I feel like we were underpaid and overworked.”

In fact, Song—mom to kids Dakota, born in 2021, and Carson, born in 2022, with fiancé Macaulay Culkin—is shocked that her time on the show hasn’t put her in the penthouse. Looking back at her years starring alongside Sprouse, his twin brother Cole Sprouse and Ashley Tisdale, the Running Point actress noted, “We basically did and the fact that we shot hundreds of episodes and our kids should be set.”

“If our show existed on any other network television channel at that time, we would have seven generations of children that would not have to worry about what they do,” the 34-year-old—dad to daughter Sylvie, 2 months, with wife Barbara Palvin—said. “The amount of income would be completely different.”

Still, Song is grateful for her time on the Disney Channel, during which she also starred in hit movies like The Ultimate Christmas Present, Get a Clue, Stuck in the Suburbs and Wendy Wu: Homecoming Warrior.

“Disney did give us a platform to be sitting here right now,” she explained. “So it’s very hard to complain about certain things.”

But, Song also added, “I look back on it and I was like oh my goodness we did actually pay them to work.”

E! News has reached out to Disney for comment but has not yet heard back.

Song is not the only star who has candidly detailed their paychecks. For more, keep reading…

The Jackass star reflected on the "comical" amount of money he was paid for doing death-defying stunts on the MTV series' first season in 2000.

"When it was all said and done, after taxes, I was paid less than $1,500 for the entire first season of Jackass," the daredevil told Playboy in June 2026. "Before the show came out, my sister kicked me out of the house. I was broke, unemployed, and homeless, and a star on this big MTV show."

Oscar winner Jennifer Lawrence was paid $25 million to star in Adam McKay’s ensemble disaster comedy Don’t Look Up. But her costar and fellow Oscar winner Leonardo DiCaprio got $30 million.

“Look, Leo brings in more box office than I do,” Lawrence told Vanity Fair for its’ December 2020/January 2021 issue. “I’m extremely fortunate and happy with my deal. But in other situations, what I have seen—and I’m sure other women in the workforce have seen as well—is that it’s extremely uncomfortable to inquire about equal pay. And if you do question something that appears unequal, you’re told it’s not gender disparity but they can’t tell you what exactly it is.”

Her sanguine attitude was hard-fought: When the disparity between Lawrence’s compensation and that of her male costars for 2013’s American Hustle was revealed in the 2014 Sony email hack, it prompted an industry-wide conversation about the gender pay gap in Hollywood.

"I'm so fortunate to have my job. My problem is not money," Lawrence told the U.K.’s Channel 4 News in 2017. "I wasn't upset that I only got this many millions for a movie. That's ridiculous. I was angry about the unfairness and inequality."

The *NSYNC alum revealed that he and his fellow bandmates JC Chasez, Joey Fatone, Chris Kirkpatrick and Justin Timberlake didn't make much money during their years with the group.

“We had a per diem: $35 a day,” he revealed on The Zach Sang Show in 2026. “Our first check was a $10,000 check after years of No. 1 albums, sellout tours. I don’t know how many millions they made off of merchandise because merchandise was insane.”

“And then they finally gave us a check for $10,000,” he recalled. “You’re like, ‘Oh, thanks.’ We should be grateful for that, been working for free for two, three years now.”

Less comparable to DiCaprio’s salary: The $60,000 “before commissions and taxes” that Jonah Hill was paid for 2013’s The Wolf of Wall Street, while the titular wolf made $10 million.

“They gave me the lowest amount of money possible,” Hill recalled on The Howard Stern Show in 2014. But it was the chance to appear in a Martin Scorsese movie, so the Moneyball alum wanted to get the deal done before anyone could change their mind.

“I would sell my house and give him all my money to work for [Scorsese],” explained Hill, who earned his second Best Supporting Actor nomination for his turn as a squirrelly substance-abusing stockbroker. “This isn't what you make money for. You do 22 Jump Street or you do other things, and you can pay your rent. I would have done anything in the world. I would do it again in a second. This isn't about money. You should do things that you care about."

According to Dylan Sprouse, his residuals from filming The Suite Life of Zack & Cody with twin brother Cole Sprouse is anything but suite.

"The only residual check I've ever received for The Suite Life at all was a crossover episode with Hannah Montana for five cents," the Disney Channel alum shared during a 2026 episode of his Wildmen podcast. "In a time where residuals would have been great, not a single paycheck for being arguably one of the most popular shows on television."

While there's no cash prize for nabbing Dancing With the Stars' mirrorball trophy, “whoever makes it to the finale, you all get paid up until then," Jenna Johnson, who won season 33 with partner Joey Graziadei, shared. "And you do get a nice bonus.”

"If you win," Johnson, who noted pro contracts are dependent on seniority, continued. "it’s not like you get a million dollars. You’re just getting a cute trophy together.” As for those who say farewell to the ballroom early, well, as she explained, "You’re guaranteed until a certain amount of weeks.” According to multiple reports, dancer salaries start at around $1,200 to $1,600 an episode, which can increase to up to of $100,000 per season. (ABC has not confirmed these reports.) On the flip side, celebrities receive a starting salary of $125,000. As they cha-cha further into the competition, stars  receive additional bonuses with the semifinalists and finalists getting paid up to $50,000 extra.

The actress seemingly confirmed that the Friends cast—including Jennifer Aniston, Courtney Cox,David Schwimmer and Matt LeBlanc—get $20 million in residuals per year from the show re-airing, quipping to The Times in April 2026 that if she had to guess why, it's “Because Phoebe Buffay was so great?"

But in actuality, she praised the talents of her costars for their performances.

“I felt I did OK, but Jennifer and Courteney? Amazing,” she raved. “David and Matt? They had me laughing so hard. And then Matthew [Perry]—he was just beyond us all.”

To hear Joe Giudice tell it, his and ex-wife Teresa Giudice's salary for season one of The Real Housewives of New Jersey was nothing to flip over. "We got paid nothing the first season," he detailed on daughter Gia Giudice's Casual Chaos podcast in August 2025. "I'll even say, it was like $25,000. It was ridiculous. But, whatever."

And the ingredientses they put into that initial fame-making season weren't cheap. "I think the first year we had that big party in my great room," the father of four reflected. "I think that show cost me $150,000 the first year."

Oprah Winfrey happily accepted only a little bit of green to star in 1985’s The Color Purple.

“They were only offering $35,000 to be in this film, and it is the best $35,000 I ever earned,” the billionaire media mogul told Essence in 2023. “It changed everything and taught me so much.”

The actress revealed that she made about $20,000 per episode of Two and a Half Men with a 5 percent raise each season, making about $43,000 for one episode in the final season.

When she scored the role of late Tejana singer Selena Quintanilla in the 1997 biopic Selena, Jennifer Lopez became the first Latina actress to earn $1 million for a film.

“I was too young and didn’t know what the hell was going on,” Lopez told Variety in 2019, reflecting on her breakout movie. “It was great they offered me a million dollars. I feel like everyone was making a statement.”

And it paved the way for her to make hundreds of millions more, though sometimes her participation doesn’t cost a thing.

“I do things because I love them,” Lopez explained to GQ in 2019. “I didn't get paid a whole bunch of money for Hustlers. I did it for free and produced it. I bank on myself, you know? Like Jenny From the Block—I do what I love."

Adrien Brody didn’t do The Brutalist for the money. Rather, he took on the role of a Hungarian architect suffering for his art in post-WWII America for $250,000 and won his second Oscar for Best Actor.

“I need a studio movie now, because I’ve poured it all into this,” Brody quipped to Variety, referring to the “barn that looks like a castle” he’s renovating in upstate New York.

“Do you guys know what they pay us?” Pete Davidson cracked to New York magazine when asked ahead of Saturday Night Live's 50th anniversary special how he spent his money when he was first hired at the age of 20 in 2014. “It’s like three grand an episode, so I think I got dinner.”

Interestingly, the salaries have remained proportional for SNL newcomers, with season one stars John Belushi, Jane Curtin, Gilda Radner, Dan Aykroyd and Chevy Chase reportedly earning $750 an episode back in 1975. Which was roughly equivalent to $3,300 in 2014, according to the Consumer Price Index Inflation calculator. (Though the $750 of 1975 is $4,428 in 2025.)

While Kenan Thompson makes a lot more than $3,000 per episode of SNL now that he’s in his record 22nd season, the former Nickelodeon star had to start somewhere.

“That first commercial when they paid me, it was $800,” the All That alum revealed in Demi Lovato‘s 2024 documentary Child Star. “I was 12 so that may as well have been a million dollars."

It turns out Gilmore Girls’ status as a beloved rewatchable classic is literally priceless.

“There really are no residuals on Netflix,” Lauren Graham, who played Lorelai Gilmore for seven seasons and then reprised the role for 2016’s Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life, said on Jimmy Kimmel Live in March 2025. “But I’ve been paid in love and appreciation.”

Feeling not so appreciated, Tommy Dorfman got specific about her 13 Reasons Why paycheck during the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strike—which was prompted in part (as was the WGA strike) by streamers like Netflix not making it a practice to pay additional compensation to cast and crew once a show had become a big hit.

"my earnings for the entire first season of 13 reasons why were $29,953.24 prior to agency and manager fees (20%) and taxes," Dorfman wrote on Threads July 24. "8 episodes over six months." She continued, “i did all of the promo and had KEY ART for this show, flew round trip from NYC to SF to shoot for every episode, was kept for days without pay/working. i barely qualified for insurance."

And, Dorfman added, “within the first 28 days of release, the show's season 1 garnered a total of 476 million view hours. this is why we strike."

Without naming names or numbers, Dax Shepard told fellow Parenthood alum Lauren Graham when she appeared on his podcast that he knew he made “among the lowest of all the actors” on their NBC drama, which ran for six seasons.

But, the Armchair Expert host stressed that he did not mind.

“Every job I had ever had in my life prior to Parenthood, I made a point to find out what everyone was making,” he said. “I'd always figure it out—either a conversation where I get it out of them or I backchannel through an agent."

So he made a point to purposely not seek out such info about his Parenthood family, which helped with enjoying the experience even when he did get an inkling of where he was on the pay pyramid.

“I got a dollar for writing the script,” George Clooney told the Los Angeles Times in 2005 about the financial strings he pulled to get his film Good Night, and Good Luck made. “I had to endorse my check for directing and turn in my acting salary. [Actor, cowriter and coproducer Grant Heslov] and I each made a buck for doing it.”

His labor of love about CBS News journalist Edward R. Murrow speaking truth to power in the 1950s had legs, though: Making his Broadway debut, Clooney wrapped his months-long stint playing Murrow in a stage adaptation of the film  in June 2025. And with the play having grossed a Broadway record (for a nonmusical) $3.3 million during a preview week before it officially opened April 3, he made a lot more than $1.

For his chilling turn as Patrick Bateman in 2000’s American Psycho, Christian Bale was paid “the absolute minimum they were legally allowed to pay me” because no one in the production really wanted to hire him except director Mary Harron, the Welsh actor told GQ in 2022.

He made so little, Bale shared, that he remembered “sitting in the makeup trailer and the makeup artists were laughing at me because I was getting paid less than any of them.”

No, the Game of Thrones cast didn't get paid $300,000 per episode, according to Emilia Clarke.

“We didn’t earn that much," she told Variety in 2026. "Can you imagine? I’d have been driving a couple of Porsches!"

However, the actress—who played Daenerys Targaryen for eight seasons between 2011 and 2019—noted that the money she made throughout the HBO show did provide her with enough financial security to pay off her parents’ mortgage.

His uncle may have been Rico, but Jon Heder confirmed in 2010 that he was “initially” only paid $1,000 for Napoleon Dynamite.

After the irreverent comedy became a sleeper hit, he was able to renegotiate for a piece of the profits, telling the New Zealand Herald, “They went a little bit higher.”

Djimon Hounsou said he’s “definitely underpaid” in Hollywood despite his prestigious list of credits, including Amistad and Blood Diamond.

"I've been in this business and making films now over two decades," the Beninese actor told CNN’s Larry Madowo in January 2025. "And still—with two Oscar nominations and been in many big blockbuster films—and yet I’m still struggling financially to make a living."

Rebel Wilson detailed in her 2024 memoir Rebel Rising that she was paid $3,500 to do Bridesmaids, “a fee that I then had to pay directly to the Screen Actors Guild to join the union. So really, I got paid nothing.”

Still, she wrote, the experience was “everything!”

And the Australian actress’ star rose ever a-ca higher, with her fee going from the SAG minimum scale of $65,000 for 2012’s Pitch Perfect to $10 million for 2017’s Pitch Perfect 3. Wilson wrote that she raked in $20 million total for the threequel, Isn’t It Romantic and The Hustle, though—reality alert—she “lost almost 50 percent to taxes, 10 percent to agents and 5 percent” to her lawyer. But even after those obligations and paying her publicist, business manager and assistant, Wilson “netted what to me was an absolute fortune.”

In late 2017, Ellen Pompeo negotiated a new Grey’s Anatomy contract for $575,000 per episode, a seven-figure signing bonus and two full backend equity points worth an estimated $6 million to $7 million.

“I’m 48 now, so I’ve finally gotten to the place where I’m OK asking for what I deserve, which is something that comes only with age,” Pompeo told The Hollywood Reporter in 2018. “Because I’m not the most ‘relevant’ actress out there. I know that’s the industry perception because I’ve been this character for 14 years. But the truth is, anybody can be good on a show season one and two. Can you be good 14 years later? Now, that’s a f--kin’ skill.”

Reflecting more recently on how she always made less than costar Patrick Dempsey, even though she was the Grey in question, Pompeo said she didn’t begrudge him his money.

But, she said on a March 2025 episode of Call Her Daddy, “Just being that I was the namesake of the show, I deserved the same and that was harder to get. I wasn't salty about him getting what he got. I was salty that they didn't value me as much as they valued him and they never will.”

Jamie Lee Curtis recalled getting paid $2,000 a week—so $8,000 in total—for 1978’s Halloween, her movie debut. “I mean,” she told Rotten Tomatoes in 2018, “nobody got paid, anything.”

Yet while the scream queen earned four figures, director John Carpenter’s friend Nick Castle felt like a king making $25 per day to share the role of Michael Myers. (It’s Anthony Moran whose face you see when the killer’s mask comes off for a freaky second, and editor Tommy Lee Wallace also logged screentime as Michael.)

“That was a lot at the time!” Castle, who attended film school at USC with Carpenter, told Vanity Fair in 2018. “You have to remember: My interest in doing the film was being on set, so I could demystify the experience of filmmaking and directing. I expected to hang around the set for no money. But hey, $25 per day, and all I had to do was wear a rubber mask.”

Taraji P. Henson earned a Best Supporting Actress Oscar nomination for 2008’s The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, but years later she was still fired up by the $150,000 she accepted to be in the movie—after producers rejected the $500,000 quote she brought to the table.

As for the film’s leads Brad Pitt and Cate Blanchett, “You don’t hear a lot of $20 million quotes anymore, but at this time that was happening,” Henson said on the Ladies First With Laura Brown podcast in 2021. “And rightfully so—I’m not saying they shouldn’t have paid Cate and Brad what they deserved.”

But, she continued, “I’m bringing a certain amount to the seat too and I felt like what I was asking at that time in my career was fair, was fair to the ticket sales that I would contribute to this big film. Wouldn’t do it.” Henson was “gutted” when they offered $100,000, she recalled. “When it was all said and done I got $150,000, but I had to swallow my pride, baby.”

Breaking it down, “I know people go, ‘$150,000, that’s a lot of money!’” Henson acknowledged. “I don’t ever want people to think that I’m ungrateful because that is not me.” But, she calculated, “Uncle Sam is going to take 50 percent of that, so now you’re left with, what? $75,000. Now before Uncle Sam takes the money, I have to pay my team before taxes, 30 percent. So once Uncle Sam takes his 75, then I got another 30 that’s coming off of that 75, so I may have made $40,000?”

While Blanchett has made plenty of money over the years, it didn’t all come from playing royal elf Galadriel in The Lord of the Rings franchise, though it grossed $2.9 billion at the worldwide box office.

“Are you kidding me? No,” she retorted on Watch What Happens Live in August 2024 when Andy Cohen guessed LOTR was her biggest paycheck. “No one got paid anything to do that movie…I mean, I basically got free sandwiches, and I got to keep my ears.”

They weren’t paid a precious amount, that is. Orlando Bloom, who played elven warrior Legolas, shared on The Howard Stern Show in 2023 that he made $175,000 for the whole trilogy.

#890. Thomas Tuchel keeps laser focus on ‘unfinished business’ with England

Head coach did not insert release clause into contract

Tuchel ‘open to everything’ including staying after Euros

Thomas Tuchel will not be going anywhere before Euro 2028. Mauricio Pochettino is expected to leave his role as the USA men’s head coach to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United, but Tuchel has not lost his passion for international football and has revealed he did not insert a release clause when he extended his deal as England’s manager this year.

It will not matter whether there is an approach from a big club before the next tournament. United can pay about £7m to get Pochettino out of his deal, but the Football Association does not have to worry about being forced to let Tuchel go. “There’s no intention [of leaving],” Tuchel said. “I signed the contract. I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business.”

Tuchel, a Champions League winner with Chelsea in 2021, did not rule out a return to club management one day. He admitted to missing “the 50 matches” a season, “these two minutes when everything is done, before the whistle goes … it’s like the best two minutes”. But while he loves the daily grind, he added there were downsides to playing every four days and there was a twinkle in his eye when he was asked about potentially staying with England beyond the European Championship.

“I am open to everything,” he said, perhaps reflecting that it is not so long ago that people were calling for his head after England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina.

The mood has improved. Tuchel sounds energised after England’s bright start to their Nations League campaign. His contract contains a performance-related clause that would have allowed the FA to sack him had England underperformed at the World Cup, but Tuchel has support from Mark Bullingham, the chief executive, and Dan Ashworth, the chief football officer.

Ashworth and Bullingham reinforced the message in person during the summer. “They made it very early in the World Cup,” Tuchel said, explaining that the backing came while the sacking clause remained active. “They just made it very clear and it comes from a place of trust, and that’s what you look for as a coach.

“I love my players. I love my staff and I have bosses who trust me. I know how to appreciate it a lot. I miss my players, and I miss my team, and I miss the 50 matches that I’m not involved in a year. But I’m desperate to win the Nations League and to try to win the Euros.”

Tuchel, who is preparing for the Nations League game at home against Croatia on Thursday night, is thinking ahead. He is gearing up for a European Championship staged mainly in England, who would also like to be chosen to host the Nations League finals next summer. “To have it here would be exciting,” Tuchel said. “First of all, we need to reach the final.”

England need one point from their final two games in Group A3 to finish in the top two and qualify for the quarter-finals in March. Victory against Croatia would give them a chance of finishing top when they visit Spain on Sunday. The Croatia game will not merely be a celebration of Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or. Wembley will watch the captain break the England men’s appearance record, but other issues are at play.

Tuchel needs Jude Bellingham to be careful given that England’s No 10 is on a booking and at risk of missing the Spain game through suspension. There are unknowns in central defence after Marc Guéhi’s withdrawal. Ezri Konsa is unavailable against Croatia and targeting a return against Spain. Tuchel, who added James Hill and Dan Burn to his squad this week, will use a new partnership against Slaven Bilic’s side.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

It is likely to be Jarell Quansah as the right centre-back while Jarrad Branthwaite could miss out to Burn on the left. “Jarrad is doing very well but it’s a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,” Tuchel said. “Dan Burn is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons where they followed in a high press.”

Burn led the team out when England trained on Wednesday. Among the group are exciting newcomers who inevitably command the attention. Tuchel has Rio Ngumoha and Josh King in attack. He is the first senior manager to work with the Bellingham brothers. Jobe Bellingham, who has impressed with his physicality and calmness on the ball, plays a deeper midfield role than Jude. Jobe is likely to start on the bench.

Tuchel wants to reconnect with the values from the previous camp. It featured England impressing in a narrow defeat by Spain, before they crushed Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka. One big highlight from the Croatia win was Alex Scott’s performance alongside Elliot Anderson in midfield.

Scott, who is out with a thigh injury, can challenge Declan Rice. The competition for places is fierce. Rice is back after missing the last camp. Tuchel said the Arsenal midfielder remained crucial.

“Declan understands the game like he’s almost a coach on the field,” Tuchel said, but a new identity is forming. It was interesting that Tuchel mentioned the young Chelsea defender Josh Acheampong, whose first call-up may not be far away. It seems Tuchel 2.0 is taking shape.

#889. Turkey-based Bates replaces Binks in Scotland squad

David Bates could add to his four Scotland caps

Centre-back David Bates could win his first cap in seven years after being added to the Scotland squad for the matches against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

Bates, playing with Amedspor in Turkey, won the last of his four Scotland caps in 2019 and replaces fellow defender Luis Binks, who has withdrawn.

As well as spells in his homeland, 30-year-old Bates has club experience in Belgium, England and Germany, with most appearances coming at Mechelen.

He has started all 11 matches this season as Amedspor sit third in the Turkish Super Lig.

All of Bates' Scotland outings came under Alex McLeish while playing for Hamburg in the 2018-19 campaign.

Luke Graham, Jack Hendry and Ryan Porteous are the other central defenders in Sebastien Pocognoli's squad, though left-back Kieran Tierney can also operate in the head coach's preferred back three.

Brondby's Binks won his first three caps during Scotland's opening four Nations League fixtures, in which they picked up four points.

North Macedonia, who travel to Hampden on Friday, have no points in the section, with Slovenia three points better off than Scotland and Monday's hosts Switzerland on maximum points.

#888. Is Taylor Swift in the Dolly Parton CMA Awards 2026 Tribute? The Truth

Ahead of the 2026 CMA Awards on Nov. 18, where Dolly Parton is set to be honored, a source confirmed to E! News whether Taylor Swift will be taking the stage.

Taylor Swift won't be honoring the life of this showgirl in Nashville.

While a tribute to Dolly Parton will be performed at the 2026 Country Music Association Awards on Nov. 18, the "Patient Zero" singer won't be feeling the magic onstage, a CMA source confirmed to E! News.

The annual award show didn't announce which honky tonk angels would be hitting all the right notes in honor of the "Jolene" singer—who died at age 80 in August after a brief battle with cancer—but Kacey Musgraves, Miranda Lambert, Cody Johnson, Ella Langley, Luke Combs and Megan Moroney are among those performing at the Bridgestone Arena.

Swift's love for Parton was like a butterfly, as soft and gentle as a sigh. And although she won't be part of the tribute, the Grammy winner never left a blank space when it came to her feelings.

"A world without Dolly doesn't feel possible, real, or right," Swift said in a statement to E! News after Parton's death in August. "She was truly the gift that kept on giving. Dolly gave us someone to look up to while encouraging us to be who we are as individuals. Somehow she was able to give us her lessons about the world gently and honestly, simultaneously, and oftentimes hilariously."

"Along with her other fans, I am so grateful for all of it," she continued. "For the melodies and lyrics she wrote that thawed even the coldest hearts. For the millions of books she provided children all over the world so that they might fall in love with stories the way she did. For the tightropes she walked so that young girls like me could grow up dreaming of joining the circus too."

And that's not to say the "Fate of Ophelia" singer hasn't paid tribute to Parton on stage. In fact, she dedicated her Video of the Year win at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards in September to the "9 to 5" singer.

"I want to thank and dedicate this award to one person, without whom this wouldn't be happening, and that person is the ultimate showgirl, Dolly Parton," Swift said while accepting the Moon Person trophy. "Every single song that she wrote, her storytelling was so vivid and so rich."

"Listening to her songs, it's like watching the best music video you have ever seen in your life every single time you hear what she has written," she added. "She handled this thing with such grace and joy and love and gratitude for the fact that she got to do this and everything that happened in her life or her career. She channeled back into love and gratitude and appreciation for her fans."

As country music fans prepare for the CMA Awards, keep reading for more sweet dedications to Parton.

Parton's younger sister shared moving insight into their special bond in her tribute.

"Every Tuesday about this time, before the sun came up and the world was still asleep, she and I, for many years, had our coffee together over the phone," she wrote on social media. "Being little farm girls we've continued to be early risers."

She added, "As she liked to say; 'shoot Tedda, we get more work done before the sun comes up than most folks do all day long!' We would catch up on gossip, as sisters do, and drink coffee and make plans, as it has always been our way"

Cyrus reflected on his longtime friendship with the "Love Is Like a Butterfly" singer.
